findings.title: Materials' 60-point lens gap signals extreme earnings hope
findings.body: Materials shows a 60-point percentile gap between its trailing (94th) and forward (34th) valuations, the widest in the table. That spread implies the market expects 133 percent earnings growth, a bet that current depressed earnings are about to inflect sharply upward.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' month-long slide contradicts its rich trailing multiple
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile dropped 38 points in a month, the steepest decline among all sectors, yet its trailing P/E sits at the 59th percentile. This divergence suggests the market is rapidly repricing defensive earnings power lower, even though reported results haven't yet validated that pessimism.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward multiple belies its earnings decline
findings.body: Real Estate trades at a 34.97 forward P/E despite an implied 4 percent earnings decline, a combination that only makes sense if analysts expect a sharp reversal. Its forward percentile of 17 is near the bottom of its five-year range, yet the multiple itself remains high in absolute terms—an unusual pairing of cheapness and stagnation.
